battle.name: 大埡寨之戰
battle.brief: 1239年冬，蒙古軍進攻南宋荊湖東路團風縣境的大埡寨山寨，志在打通鄂州至黃州一線的水陸交通。宋方由京湖制置使孟珙主持防禦，守軍據險死守，並仿蒙古攻城所用的配重投石車反製其攻城器械，攻城車與雲梯多毀於寨下；蒙古圍攻數月不下，終以糧援不繼退去。卡面這件配重投石車，是這場攻防的關鍵。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 這場戰爭是蒙古大汗國與南宋在荊湖東路的一次攻防，時間在1239年，即宋嘉熙三年、蒙古窩闊台汗在位第十一年之冬。蒙古一方是成吉思汗建立的帝國所帶來的鐵騎集團：兵制以十進位的怯薛為骨干，攻城則靠從中亞徵發的回回（穆斯林）工匠操作配重投石車，軍中另有漢地降人充任向导、匠戶與攻城技師；行軍分為偵察、圍城、攻寨三段，糧秣多沿漢水與長江水路由北方運來。1235年之後蒙古分道南侵，西路入四川，中路趨河南，東路直指荊襄，大埡寨正處在這條東路攻勢的外圍。南宋一方是以襄陽、郢州、復州、黃州為骨架的荊襄防區，主政者是京湖制置使孟珙，輔以各州軍統制、沿江舟師與山寨守兵；孟珙沿用前任余玠在湖北與四川確立的築城方針，把防禦重心放在山嶺上的城寨，以山勢代替平原城池，寨中蓄水可通舟船，糧道因此不易被斷。兩軍的指揮體系都極簡：蒙古一側由大汗與其弟蒙哥在北方的軍令統轄，前線分遣隊指揮者的姓名在漢文史料中多有省略；宋軍一側由制置司逐級發令，寨中守軍歸當地守將率領。雙方兵種都以騎兵為核心，但攻防的技術框架不同：蒙古靠器械強行破城，宋軍靠地勢與器械反制拖延。
countriesEn: This war was an attack and a defence between the Mongol khanate and the Southern Song in the Jinghu circuit, fought in the winter of 1239, the third year of Jiaxi in the Song calendar and the eleventh year of the reign of the Great Khan Ogedei. On the Mongol side was the cavalry empire built by Chinggis Khan: its backbone was the decimal keshig, its siege work was run by Huihui, that is Muslim, engineers recruited in Central Asia, and its ranks also held Chinese and Central Asian deserters serving as guides, craftsmen and siege technicians. Its advance was organised in three stages, reconnaissance, investment and the storming of the fort, and its grain came down the Han and the Yangtze from the north. After 1235 the Mongols marched south in several columns, one into Sichuan, one towards Henan and one straight at Jingxiang, and Dayuan lay on the outer fringe of that eastern column. The Song side was the Jingxiang defence built on the framework of Xiangyang, Yingzhou, Fuzhou and Huangzhou, administered by the Jinghu Circuit Commissioner Meng Gong and supported by the circuit commanders of each prefecture, the river squadrons and the garrisons of the mountain forts. Meng Gong followed the policy of building forts that Yu Jie had established in Hubei and Sichuan, moving the weight of the defence from the plain to the ridges so that the terrain took the place of the walls of a level city, and each fort held a pond or a channel through which boats could pass, which made the supply route hard to cut. Both command systems were very simple. On the Mongol side the orders came from the Great Khan and from his brother Mongke in the north, and the names of the commanders of the detachments sent into the field are mostly omitted in the Chinese sources. On the Song side the orders ran down from the circuit office, and the garrison of each fort obeyed its own commander. Cavalry formed the core of both armies, but the technical frame of attack and defence was different: the Mongols broke cities with machines, the Song bought time with terrain and with machines turned against those machines.
people: 留下姓名的多數是宋方。孟珙（1195—1246），字玉汝，隨州人，是這條荊襄防線的實際主持者。他的父親孟宗政原為岳飛部將，鎮守隨州多年，卒於1234年；孟珙自1234年隨趙葵北伐、收復蔡州起轉戰東西，先後參與收復襄、樊、郢、復、江陵，約1237年前後出任京湖制置使，掌荊襄兵政與軍需。他在大埡寨之役中的做法，是先用守禦消耗敵軍銳氣，再以砲反製蒙古的攻城器械，這是宋軍成規模地把配重投石車用來打擊敵方攻城武器的早期實例之一。另一位重要人物是余玠（1198—1253），字義仁，衢州龍游人，1234至1236年間出任湖北制置使（起任年份各書記載不一），在鄂北鄂西一帶推行築城，提出因山為城、因城設關的防禦原則；1236年他調任四川制置使，在合州東山修築釣魚城，把這套山城體系推到極致，雖然大埡寨交戰時他遠在川陝，荊襄各寨的形制仍出自他定下的路子。與孟珙同時在荊北的前線將領還有趙葵等人，趙葵曾統兵北伐，是1230年代中期宋軍在河南一線的主帥。蒙古方面留下姓名的，多是統帥：1239年主持全局的是大汗窩闊台，在前線操持南線軍事的是其弟蒙哥；蒙哥在1236年科斷之變中清洗了一批掌管簿籍稅賦的官員，汗廷內部的裂痕由此加深，前線戰功在往後數年成為各方爭功的資本。至於包圍大埡寨的分遣隊由誰率領、寨中守將姓甚名誰，漢文史料都沒有留下可靠記載，只能說命令出自主持京湖軍務的孟珙。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive belong to the Song side. Meng Gong, who lived from 1195 to 1246, courtesy name Yuru, a native of Suizhou, was the man who actually ran this line of the Jingxiang front. His father, Meng Zongzheng, had begun as a soldier under Yue Fei, had held Suizhou for years against the Jin and died in 1234. Meng Gong himself first came to notice in the campaigns of 1234 to 1236: he served with Zhao Kui in the recovery of Caizhou, then took part in the taking back of Xiang, Fan, Ying, Fu and Jiangling, and from about 1237 onward he held the office of Jinghu Circuit Commissioner, with control of the troops and the supply of Jingxiang. His way of fighting at Dayuan was to spend the enemy's strength on the defences first and then to answer the besiegers' own siege machines with stone thrown by his own engines, and Dayuan is one of the earliest cases in which the Song used the counterweight trebuchet in a set way to break up attacking equipment. The other important figure is Yu Jie, who lived from 1198 to 1253, courtesy name Yiren, a native of Longyou in Quzhou. Between 1234 and 1236 he served as Hubei Circuit Commissioner, the exact year of his appointment differing from book to book, and he set about building forts in northern and western Hubei, setting out the principle of making the hill into the fort and the fort into the pass. In 1236 he was transferred to the post of Sichuan Circuit Commissioner and raised the fort of Diaoyu on the eastern heights of Hezhou, carrying that system of mountain forts to its extreme. Though Yu Jie was thousands of li away in Sichuan when Dayuan was fought, the shape of the Jingxiang forts still followed the line he had laid down. Among the Song commanders on the northern Jing front at the same time was Zhao Kui, who had led the northern expeditions and was a commander of the Song armies on the Henan front in the middle of the 1230s. The names that survive on the Mongol side are those of the commanders in chief: in 1239 the overall direction was in the hands of the Great Khan Ogedei, while his brother Mongke managed the southern effort at the front. In the affair known as the Kedan purge of 1236 Mongke had put to death a set of officials who kept the registers of taxation, and the rift inside the khanate widened from that, with the results of the front serving in the years after as capital in the struggle for credit. As for who led the detachment that surrounded Dayuan, and what the name of the commander inside the fort was, the Chinese histories record neither reliably; the orders can only be taken to have come from Meng Gong, who then held the military affairs of Jinghu.
kits: 卡面上這件配重投石車，是這場攻防裡真正決定距離的兵器。所謂配重投石車，長臂一端懸著裝滿石塊的配重箱，另一端裝短臂與兜索，發射時以配重下墜帶動長臂甩起，把石彈拋向遠方；相對於早期要靠人力反覆拉拽的扭力投石車，它可以靠一次釋放把百斤上下的石彈送出數百步，砸在城牆、垛口與守軍最密集之處。歐洲中世紀的攻城記錄裡它是常見的攻城器械，所以兵器卡把它歸在歐洲兵器的名下；但在1239年的中國，蒙古人帶來的是另一個來源的同一種機械，即中亞回回工匠操作的回回炮。回回炮在1236年之後蒙古攻襄陽、郢州的戰事中已經出現，宋軍在孟珙主持下仿其制，把砲位擺在寨牆之後與兩翼，先以石彈打擊蒙古軍的雲梯、撞車與帳篷式攻城車，再用同樣的武器反擊其本陣，攻城器械一批批地壞在牆下。除了擲石機，蒙古軍在寨外還備有木製攻城車與覆以牛皮的活動攻城塔，以及以木為架、以皮為帳、可移動到城下的鵝車；拋射的石彈同時是攻擊武器與心理震懾。守方能倚仗的還有弓弩與新興火器：宋廷在1230年代已開始使用震天雷一類的爆炸物，並以強弩射程覆蓋城下通道；而孟珙最看重的仍是水路上的補給能力——山寨四面山巒、寨中可蓄水通船，糧食由漢水與長江的水師輸送，敵軍即使合圍也切不斷糧道，這正是釣城體系的核心。蒙古軍隊本身仍以輕騎為主，攻城卻需從北方押送大量木料、人力與糧秣，馬匹的補充同樣要靠遠道輸送；在荊北多水多雨的地理裡，這是他們最難補的弱點。
kitsEn: The counterweight trebuchet on the card is the piece of equipment that actually decided the distance in this fight. A counterweight trebuchet carries a long arm with a counterweight box full of stones hung at one end, and a short arm with a sling at the other; when the machine is released, the falling weight drives the long arm over and throws the stone far away. Compared with the earlier traction trebuchet, which had to be hauled back by manpower again and again, it could send a stone of a hundred jin or more several hundred paces in a single shot, and it landed on the walls, on the battlements and on the places where the defenders were most densely posted. In the siege records of medieval Europe it was a common instrument of a breached town, which is why the weapon card places it among the European arms; but in the China of 1239 the Mongols had brought the same machine from a different source, the counterweight trebuchet worked by the Huihui, that is Muslim, engineers of Central Asia. The Huihui pao had already appeared in the Mongol sieges of Xiangyang and Yingzhou after 1236, and under Meng Gong the Song copied it, set the engines behind the fort wall and on the flanks, first broke up the Mongol ladders, rams and tented siege vehicles with stone, and then used the same weapons against the mass of the besiegers, so that the attacking equipment was destroyed in batches below the wall. Besides the throwing engines the Mongols brought up wooden siege cars, mobile towers sheathed in hide, and the goose car, a timber frame covered with leather that could be moved up to the foot of the wall; the stones thrown were at once a weapon and a shock to the nerves. What the defenders could rely on were the bow and the crossbow and the newer fire weapons: the Song court had already begun using explosive devices of the thunder-crash bomb type in the 1230s, and strong crossbows covered the approaches below the wall with their range. What Meng Gong valued above all was still the ability to resupply by water. The forts stood among mountains with a pond inside that boats could reach, and the grain came in by the squadrons on the Han and the Yangtze, so that even a complete investment could not cut the supply line, and that was the core of the system of the fishing forts. The Mongol army itself remained light cavalry in essence, yet a siege required a great deal of timber, manpower and fodder to be brought down from the north, and the horses had to be replenished over the same long road. In the wet and watery country north of the Jing that was the weakness they could least repair.
tactics: 這場攻防的樣板，是宋人在荊襄一線摸索出來的山城抵禦法。築城的前提是放棄在平原上與蒙古騎兵爭鋒，改為在山嶺與河谷的險要處立寨：寨牆順山脊修築，充分利用高差；寨門不設在平緩的正面，而設在只有一條路可通的狹窄處；寨中開鑿水池或引水成塘，把糧食由船運入，敵人就算封住陸路，水路仍在；寨外再挖壕溝、置拒馬、堆鹿角，把蒙古騎兵最擅長的衝鋒速度削掉。進攻方蒙古的做法是先偵察、再分割、最後攻寨：以輕騎遮斷寨外道路與援兵，以小股部隊逐次拔除外圍小寨與烽燧，逼宋軍分兵，然後把攻城器械集中到主攻方向連續衝擊，石彈覆蓋牆頭，帳篷攻城車與雲梯同時貼上城牆，梯上的兵在器械掩護下攀城。守方的反制是所謂以砲制砲：孟珙把仿製的配重投石車分置寨牆兩側與後方，不求直射城頭，而求覆蓋蒙古攻城器械集結與展開的地面，一發石彈落下，鵝車、撞車與雲梯的毀損會直接打亂攻勢的節奏；弓弩手則趁器械受損、敵軍陣形混亂的時機出寨反擊。圍攻拖得越久，蒙古軍的糧道與援軍調度就越吃緊：荊北多雨多水，遠道而來的攻城木料與秣草難以就地補充，蒙古騎兵又不敢在宋軍水師控制的江漢水道上久留。於是這類戰役的典型結局往往是：蒙古軍攻之數月不能下，攻城器械損耗殆盡，糧援不繼，最後退兵；宋軍則以一座山寨為代價，換取整條防線的時間。這也是大埡寨之役最可能的面貌。
tacticsEn: The model of this fight was the defence by mountain fort that the Song worked out along the Jingxiang line. The first premise of building forts was to give up meeting the Mongol horse in the open plain and to set the fort on a ridge or in a defile: the wall followed the spine of the hill and used the differences in height; the gate was not put on the gentle side but on a narrow place where only one road led up; a pool was dug inside the fort or water was led in, so that grain could be brought in by boat, and even if the enemy sealed the land route the water route remained; outside the wall a ditch was dug, chevaux-de-frise were set and caltrops were scattered, to take the speed out of the Mongol charge, which was the one thing their horse was best at. The attacker's Mongol method was to reconnoitre, to divide, and then to assault the fort. Light horse cut the roads outside the fort and the roads of the relieving force; small detachments removed the smaller forts and the beacon towers one by one so as to force the Song to divide its troops; and then the siege engines were concentrated on the main axis of attack, the stone shot covering the wall while the tented cars and the ladders came up to the masonry at the same time, the men on the ladders climbing under cover of the engines. The defence answered with engine against engine. Meng Gong set his copied counterweight trebuchets on both flanks of the fort and in the rear; he did not aim at the wall head but at the ground where the Mongol siege machines assembled and deployed, and a single stone falling there broke the rhythm of the assault, because the goose cars, the rams and the ladders were lost; archers and crossbowmen then came out to strike while the enemy was disordered. The longer the siege lasted, the harder the Mongols found it to feed the army and to move reinforcements. The country north of the Jing was wet and full of water, the timber and the fodder brought over a long road could not be replaced on the spot, and their horse dared not linger on the Han and Yangtze waterways patrolled by the Song squadrons. The typical outcome of such a siege was therefore this: the Mongols attacked for months without taking the fort, their siege equipment was used up, their supply failed, and at last they withdrew; the Song paid with one fort and bought time for the whole line. That is the most probable shape of the battle at Dayuan.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類，可靠程度不同。第一類是年表：1239年，宋嘉熙三年，干支己亥，蒙古大汗窩闊台在位第十一年；這一年蒙古在南線的主要動作是回師四川、第二次深入荊北，而1236年蒙古第一次攻襄陽時宋蒙曾在鄂州一線議和，宋付出歲幣、蒙古取得借道攻宋與攻蜀的便利，是理解大埡寨之役的前提。第二類是文獻可查的兵力與工程量級：蒙古在荊北的攻勢，每次投入的是數千至一萬餘人的分遣隊與攻城部隊，具體數字在漢文史料中多被省略；配重投石車每次發射的石彈，重者達百餘斤，架設一座砲位需數十至數百人配合，攻城用的鵝車、雲梯與撞車常以數十具計，這些是當時攻城器械的常見量級，具體數目各家記載不一，不宜當作定數。第三類是地理：團風在長江北岸，東距鄂州、西距黃州城各數十里，寨址在城北山嶺，扼漢水下游與長江之交，控江漢兩條水道；蒙古若取此處，可自鄂州、黃州西進，截斷宋在荊襄的南北轉運。第四類是後人追述與今人研究：這場戰役在宋人筆下記載極為簡略，交戰的具體日期、雙方陣亡與俘獲數字多不可考；學界通常把襄、樊、郢、復、壽昌一線的城寨，視為孟珙在1236至1240年間陸續修復與新建的成果，但各城修建的先後與規模，文獻並無完整清單。第五類是後來可見的痕跡：團風一帶至今仍留有宋代山寨與城堡的地名與遺址，考古報告零散，難以把某一段城垣直接指認為大埡寨本身。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several classes of very different reliability. The first is the chronology: 1239, the third year of Jiaxi in the Song, the year jihai in the sexagenary cycle, the eleventh year of the Great Khan Ogedei. The main Mongol action on the southern front that year was the return to Sichuan and a second deep push into Jingbei, and the fact that in 1236, when the Mongols first attacked Xiangyang, the Song and the Mongols negotiated at the Ezhou line, the Song paying in silver and silk while the Mongols obtained the right to pass through Song territory and to attack Shu, is the premise for understanding the battle at Dayuan. The second class is the strength and the scale of works the texts do record. The detachments the Mongols sent into Jingbei on each push were in the thousands to a little over ten thousand men together with the siege corps, though the exact figures are mostly omitted in the Chinese sources. The stones thrown by a counterweight trebuchet weighed as much as a hundred jin and more, the setting up of one engine required the work of several tens to several hundreds of men, and the goose cars, ladders and rams used in a siege were commonly counted by the tens. These are the usual orders of magnitude for such machines at the time; the specific numbers differ from book to book and should not be treated as fixed. The third class is geography: Tuanfeng lies on the north bank of the Yangtze, some tens of li east of Ezhou and some tens of li west of the city of Huangzhou, with the site of the fort on the hills north of the town, commanding the meeting of the lower Han and the Yangtze and controlling both waterways. If the Mongols had taken it they could have advanced from Ezhou and Huangzhou and cut the north-south carrying trade of the Song in Jingxiang. The fourth class is later reconstruction and modern study: the record of this battle in Song writings is extremely brief, and the exact dates of the fighting and the figures for dead and captured on both sides cannot be checked. Scholars generally treat the line of forts at Xiang, Fan, Ying, Fu and Shouchang as the result of the repair and building that Meng Gong carried on between 1236 and 1240, but there is no complete list of the order and the scale in which the various forts were raised. The fifth class is what can still be seen: around Tuanfeng there remain place names and traces of Song fortresses, the excavation reports are scattered, and no stretch of wall can be identified with certainty as Dayuan itself.
cause: 打起來的原因有遠有近。遠因是蒙古的西征已經完成：1227年滅西夏，1230年代中期平定花剌子模故地，蒙古已把作戰經驗、中亞工匠與攻城器械一併帶到東亞，1235年之後分道南侵，東路直指荊襄。近因是宋的戰略收縮與自身的失誤：端平北伐在1234至1236年間接連三次出師，糧道不繼而全線崩潰，北伐主力化為潰散之師，國力由此空虛；宋廷在荊襄雖有孟珙、余玠一批能戰之臣，整體上卻只能退守。技術層面的原因最直接：蒙古的攻城能力在荊北屢受挫折之後，需要逐點拔除宋朝的山城據點；大埡寨扼江漢水道，是宋在湖北的交通與防禦骨架上的一環，拔掉它，下一步就是鄂州與黃州；而荊北多山多水，正好讓宋軍的守禦技術發揮作用，蒙古遂不惜以大量攻城器械與人力去換。政治層面，1236年科斷之變之後，蒙古內部對稅賦與權位的爭執未平，前線的戰果被各方當作立功與爭位的資本，主戰的意願反而更強。還有一層常被忽略的算計：1235至1236年宋蒙鄂州議和時，蒙古取得歲幣與借道攻宋的便利，宋廷用錢財買來的時間不到兩年便用盡，1239年蒙古再度南下，戰線又回到荊襄，而大埡寨正好立在鄂州、黃州之間的水陸咽喉上。
causeEn: There were distant causes and immediate ones. The distant cause was that the Mongol western conquest was over: the Xia had been destroyed in 1227, the lands of former Khwarazm had been settled in the middle of the 1230s, and the Mongols now brought to East Asia the experience, the craftsmen of Central Asia and the siege engines of that campaign, so that after 1235 they marched south in several columns, one of them going straight at Jingxiang. The immediate cause lay in the contraction of the Song's strategy and in its own mistakes. The Duanping northern expeditions were launched three times in succession between 1234 and 1236, ran out of supplies and collapsed from end to end, the field army was turned into a routed mob, and the state was left hollow. The Song court had in Jingxiang able commanders such as Meng Gong and Yu Jie, but in the whole it could only hold what it had. The most direct reason was technical. After being checked repeatedly in Jingbei, the Mongol siege capability had to take the Song's hill forts one at a time, and Dayuan commanded the waterways of the Han and the Yangtze and was one link in the transport and defensive frame of the Song in Hubei; taking it opened the way to Ezhou and Huangzhou. The country north of the Jing, full of hills and water, was exactly the terrain on which the Song defence worked best, so the Mongols were willing to spend engines and men on it. At the political level, the purge at Kedan in 1236 left the quarrel over taxation and authority inside the Mongol camp unsettled, and the results of the front were read by the competing hands as capital for merit and for influence, which strengthened rather than weakened the will to fight. There is also a calculation often left out. When the Song and the Mongols negotiated at Ezhou in 1235 and 1236, the Mongols obtained silver and silk and the right to pass through Song territory in order to attack the Song, and the time the Song bought with money lasted less than two years. In 1239 the Mongols came south again, the front was back in Jingxiang, and Dayuan stood precisely on the water and land throat between Ezhou and Huangzhou.
impact: 就當時而言，這場攻防的意義不在規模，而在示範：蒙古在南線遇到的第一座啃不下來的山城，出現在一個蒙古騎兵最不舒服的地理環境裡，結果是宋軍靠地形、靠水路上的糧道、靠一種可以複製的攻城器械反制，把蒙古的攻勢頂了回去。大埡寨這類山寨在1230年代末到1240年代被一批批地修起來，構成荊襄防線的骨架，此後二十多年蒙古在荊襄一線始終未能整體突破，直到1270年代襄樊失守，整條線才崩解，而這二十多年的時間，正是這一類小城寨一個一個頂出來的。工程上的刺激更為長遠：蒙古帶來回回炮，宋人仿造之，此後數十年裡配重投石車在中國的攻防體系中站穩了位置，明代兵書所收的各式火砲圖樣裡仍能看出這條譜系；而蒙古自身後來把同一種機械帶往西亞，1258年攻巴格達、1268年攻阿勒頗時使用的攻城砲，正是這類配重投石車，歐亞兩端的工程技術在同一場宋元戰爭裡互相傳遞。對地方來說，團風、黃州一線的寨堡體系把鄉村、糧倉與兵站編進戰爭，兵農合一的地方防衛在元代成為蒙古統治者難以根除的問題，這是元代州縣與軍鎮長期並存的背景之一。至於大埡寨本身，它在宋元之際留下的名字更多地留在地方志與地名裡，戰場細節至今仍難以一一對應。
impactEn: For the time, the meaning of this fight lay not in its size but in the example it set. The first hill fort the Mongols could not chew on their southern front stood in the one landscape most hostile to Mongol cavalry, and the Song held it with terrain, with a supply route kept open by water, and with a kind of siege engine that could be copied, and turned the Mongol assault back. Forts of the Dayuan type were built one after another between the late 1230s and the 1240s, and they formed the skeleton of the Jingxiang line. For more than twenty years the Mongols could not break that line as a whole, and it was not until the fall of Xiangfan in the 1270s that it came apart, and those more than twenty years were bought for a fort at a time. The stimulation in engineering was longer lived. The Mongols brought the Huihui pao, the Song copied it, and the counterweight trebuchet held its place in the Chinese art of attack and defence for the decades that followed; the plates of the various gun types in the Ming military books still show that lineage. The Mongols themselves carried the same machine further west, and the siege guns used at Baghdad in 1258 and at Aleppo in 1268 were counterweight trebuchets of this family, so that the engineering of the two ends of Eurasia was exchanged in the course of one and the same Song-Yuan war. Locally, the system of forts along the Tuanfeng and Huangzhou lines drew the villages, the granaries and the depots into the war, and the fusion of soldier and farmer in local defence became a problem the Mongol rulers could never root out; that is part of the background to the way prefecture and military town existed side by side under the Yuan. As for Dayuan itself, its name survives in local gazetteers and in place names rather than in battle narrative, and the details of the field remain hard to match to any one site.
result: 結果的輪廓是清楚的：1239年冬，蒙古軍進攻團風大埡寨未能得手，攻城器械在宋軍以配重投石車為主的反擊下損毀殆盡，圍攻在若干個月後因糧援不繼、器械難以補充而中止，蒙古軍退去；宋軍守住了山寨，荊襄防線得以延續。必須說明的是，這一戰的細節在漢文史料中只剩下零星數語，交戰的具體日期、蒙古分遣隊的番將姓名、寨中守將、雙方死傷與俘獲數字，都沒有可靠的記載；所謂宋軍以回回炮擊毀蒙古攻城器械的說法，與《宋史·孟珙傳》等書記載的孟珙在襄、郢一線仿製蒙古攻城砲並用之反擊其器械的作法是同一套東西，把它放在大埡寨之役，與宋廷當時在荊襄整體的守禦方針、與蒙古在1239年再度深入荊北的部署都能對得上，但仍應視為合理的推論而非確證。往後看，這場戰役的真正結果有兩層：短期看，宋軍以一座山寨為代價，守住了江漢交通的一段節點，讓蒙古的第二次深入荊北空手而回；長期看，它證明了築城守禦能把蒙古的攻勢拖成消耗戰，卻改變不了宋蒙之間的實力差距，蒙古退回北方，十年後又回來，1270年代襄樊失守，荊襄防線終於被壓垮，大埡寨式的山城守禦在全國範圍內也隨之崩解。一場沒有留下多少文字的戰役，卻正好立在兩個時代的接縫上。
resultEn: The outline of the outcome is clear. In the winter of 1239 the Mongol attack on the fort of Dayuan at Tuanfeng did not succeed. The siege equipment was destroyed in the main by the counterweight trebuchets of the Song, the siege dragged on for some months and was abandoned when the supplies ran short and the engines could no longer be replaced, and the Mongols withdrew; the Song held the fort and the Jingxiang line was preserved. It has to be said that the details of this fight survive in the Chinese histories only in scattered phrases: the exact dates of the fighting, the name of the Mongol commander of the detachment, the name of the Song commander inside the fort, and the figures for the dead and captured on both sides are all without reliable record. The account that the Song destroyed the Mongol siege equipment with the Huihui pao is of a piece with what the Songshi biography of Meng Gong records, that is his copying of the Mongols' throwing engines on the Xiang and Ying lines and turning them against the enemy's own machines. Set in the battle at Dayuan, it fits both the defensive policy the Song court was following in Jingxiang and the Mongol deployments of 1239, but it should be treated as a reasonable inference rather than a certainty. Looking back, the true result of the battle has two layers. In the short term, the Song paid with one fort and kept one section of the transport of the river system, and the Mongols' second deep push into Jingbei came back empty. In the long term, it proved that a defence of built forts could turn a Mongol assault into a war of attrition, but it did not change the balance of strength between Song and Mongol. The Mongols withdrew to the north, came back ten years later, took Xiangfan in the 1270s, and the Jingxiang line was broken at last, and the defence by mountain forts of the Dayuan kind collapsed with it across the country. A battle that left few words behind stands exactly on the seam between two eras.
